title: The Rampant Problem of Pregnancy Discrimination, Part 2

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上对精选采访进行现场直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, part two of the Times investigation into pregnancy discrimination.
sentences.zh: 今天，播出《纽约时报》关于怀孕歧视调查的第二部分。

sentences.en: The subtle sidelining of pregnant women and mothers in corporate America.
sentences.zh: 美国企业界对孕妇和母亲的无形边缘化。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, June 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月27日，星期三。

sentences.en: Erin, did you always know that you wanted kids?
sentences.zh: 艾琳，你一直都知道自己想要孩子吗？

sentences.en: I would say no.
sentences.zh: 我会说没有。

sentences.en: I think there was a point in time where I was going to be much more career-focused and kind of thought, well, maybe the kids thing isn't for me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得曾有一段时间，我更专注于职业发展，甚至想过，也许生孩子并不适合我。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, while working on this investigation into pregnancy discrimination, I met this woman, Erin Murphy.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，在进行这项关于怀孕歧视的调查时，我遇到了这位女性，艾琳·墨菲。

sentences.en: Natalie Kytroeff covers the economy for the Times.
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉·基特罗夫负责《纽约时报》的经济报道。

sentences.en: She works in commodities trading in New York.
sentences.zh: 她在纽约从事大宗商品交易工作。

sentences.en: Basically buying and selling commodities that could be anything from metals or oil or cotton or things like that.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是买卖大宗商品，可以是金属、石油、棉花之类的大宗商品。

sentences.en: Specifically, she works with crude oil traders on a big trading floor, and she coordinates the movement of oil from one place to the other.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，她在大型交易大厅与原油交易员一起工作，负责协调石油从一个地方到另一个地方的调运。

sentences.en: It's a well-paid job with a six-figure salary and a bonus in an office tower.
sentences.zh: 这是一份薪水优厚的工作，位于一栋办公大楼里，不仅有六位数的高薪，还有奖金。

sentences.en: And while I was in school, I got this job at a company called Louis Dreyfuss.
sentences.zh: 我在上学的时候，就得到了这家名为路易达孚的公司的工作。

sentences.en: And then she moved to Goldman Sachs.
sentences.zh: 后来她跳槽到了高盛。

sentences.en: And eventually, she landed at Glencore, which is the world's largest commodities trading firm.
sentences.zh: 最后，她落脚于嘉能可，这是全球最大的大宗商品交易公司。

sentences.en: At first, it felt like this is great.
sentences.zh: 起初，感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: I can succeed here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里能成功。

sentences.en: I can be great here.
sentences.zh: 我在这里能有一番作为。

sentences.en: And things are going well.
sentences.zh: 一切都很顺利。

sentences.en: She's getting good reviews.
sentences.zh: 她得到了很好的评价。

sentences.en: Excellent reviews.
sentences.zh: 极好的评价。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, I was given shares to the company because I was...
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，公司分发给我股份，因为我是……

sentences.en: As a reward.
sentences.zh: 作为奖励。

sentences.en: As a reward.
sentences.zh: 作为奖励。

sentences.en: So I was being compensated for what I was being told, that I was an excellent employee, I was invaluable, I was helping make my traders successful.
sentences.zh: 所以我得到的报酬印证了他们对我的评价：我是一名极优秀的员工，我是不可或缺的，我在协助交易员取得成功。

sentences.en: I never once was told anything to the contrary.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有听任何人说过相反的话。

sentences.en: But there was one thing that was less than ideal.
sentences.zh: 但有一点不太理想。

sentences.en: The oil industry is a very, like, old-school boys club.
sentences.zh: 石油行业是一个非常传统的老派兄弟会。

sentences.en: I mean, if you came to my office and you looked at who the traders were and who the people in power were, you would notice right away they're predominantly white male.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你来到我的办公室，看看谁是交易员，谁是掌权者，你会立即注意到他们绝大多数是白人男性。

sentences.en: And then there's a lot of, you know, regular banter, you know, I guess, locker room talk.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，有很多日常的玩笑，我想，就是更衣室式的闲聊。

sentences.en: So men, they're talking about women.
sentences.zh: 所以男人们，他们在谈论女性。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that I realized early on that if I wanted to be liked, if I wanted to move on, if I wanted to be given opportunities, I had to be okay with it.
sentences.zh: 我想我早就意识到，如果我想被人喜欢，如果我想晋升，如果我想获得机会，我就必须接受这一切。

sentences.en: You know, allow it to happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，默认它发生。

sentences.en: Despite all that, she's settling into this job.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，她还是在这个岗位上安顿下来。

sentences.en: And in the meantime, things are changing for her outside of work.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，她的工作之外的生活也在发生变化。

sentences.en: She gets married.
sentences.zh: 她结婚了。

sentences.en: She starts thinking about having kids.
sentences.zh: 她开始考虑生孩子。

sentences.en: And in 2014, she gets pregnant.
sentences.zh: 2014年，她怀孕了。

sentences.en: And so I was pretty nervous about being pregnant.
sentences.zh: 所以我对怀孕感到相当紧张。

sentences.en: I was pretty nervous about how that was going to impact my career.
sentences.zh: 我很担心这会对我的职业生涯产生什么影响。

sentences.en: So I've waited a long time to tell work.
sentences.zh: 所以我拖了很久才把消息告诉公司。

sentences.en: I waited until 18 weeks until I told work.
sentences.zh: 我直到怀孕第18周才告诉公司。

sentences.en: And since I had a very friendly relationship with the head trader of my desk, I pulled him aside and I let him know.
sentences.zh: 由于我和我所在交易台的首席交易员关系很融洽，我把他拉到一旁，把这个消息告诉了他。

sentences.en: I said, I'm having a baby.
sentences.zh: 我说，我要当妈妈了。

sentences.en: And I said, I'm 18 weeks long.
sentences.zh: 我说，我已经怀孕18周了。

sentences.en: And he asked, why did you wait so long to tell me?
sentences.zh: 他问，为什么这么晚才告诉我？

sentences.en: And I said, I'm very concerned that this is going to impact my career.
sentences.zh: 我说，我很担心这会影响我的职业生涯。

sentences.en: And his response was, well, it won't impact it, but it will definitely plateau it.
sentences.zh: 他的回答是，嗯，它不会影响你的职业发展，但它绝对会让你的职业生涯进入平台期。

sentences.en: Plateau it.
sentences.zh: 进入平台期。

sentences.en: That's another, it's a fancy way of saying.
sentences.zh: 那是另一种说法，一种委婉的说法。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Your career is going to stay where it is now.
sentences.zh: 你的职业生涯将停留在现在的水平。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I was immediately, I guess, defensive to prove to him that it wasn't going to change me.
sentences.zh: 我当时立刻，我想，本能地想要反驳，向他证明这不会改变我。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But in the back of your mind, did you believe him?
sentences.zh: 但在内心深处，你相信他的话吗？

sentences.en: I think I still had hope.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时仍然抱有希望。

sentences.en: I think I still felt like, well, he doesn't know me.
sentences.zh: 我想我仍然觉得，好吧，他不了解我。

sentences.en: You know, maybe that happened with other women, but I'm going to work even harder.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许那种事发生在其他女性身上，但我会更加努力工作。

sentences.en: I'm going to put in 10 times the effort that I've already put in so that I can prove it different.
sentences.zh: 我要付出比以往多十倍的努力，来证明情况会不同。

sentences.en: I can prove him wrong and maybe, you know, they'll see.
sentences.zh: 我可以证明他是错的，也许，你知道，他们会看到的。

sentences.en: Women can be mothers and have great careers.
sentences.zh: 女性既可以成为母亲，也可以拥有伟大的职业生涯。

sentences.en: To me, it was very important that I didn't get, I don't know, stereotyped, I guess.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，非常重要的一点是，我不要被，我不知道，被脸谱化、贴上标签吧。

sentences.en: And what is the stereotype that you're afraid of?
sentences.zh: 你害怕的刻板印象是什么？

sentences.en: I think that it's sort of known that once you're a mother.
sentences.zh: 我想大家都知道，一旦你成了母亲。

sentences.en: You just did air quotes.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚做了个打引号的手势。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Mother.
sentences.zh: 母亲。

sentences.en: It's a game changer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨变。

sentences.en: It's just, you're different.
sentences.zh: 就是，你变得不一样了。

sentences.en: You know, you're not on the same playing field anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不再处于同一起跑线上了。

sentences.en: And I just, I wanted, I thought I could be different.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我想要，我以为我可以与众不同。

sentences.en: You know, I thought that I would find a way to be able to be a mom, but to also be a woman who would have an amazing growing career.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我以为我会找到一种方法，既能当妈妈，又能成为一个职业生涯蒸蒸日上的女性。

sentences.en: Natalie, what happens to Erin Murphy after she has her baby?
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉，艾琳·墨菲生完孩子后发生了什么？

sentences.en: So she has her baby, a boy, and after a few months of maternity leave, she's getting ready to go back to work.
sentences.zh: 她生下了一个男孩，在休了几个月产假后，她正准备重返工作岗位。

sentences.en: And she's arranging everything so that having this kid does not derail her career.
sentences.zh: 她把一切都安排妥当，好让这个孩子的出生不会毁了她的职业生涯。

sentences.en: She gets child care starting at 7 a.m.
sentences.zh: 她安排了早上7点开始的育儿托管。

sentences.en: Her husband's on board for pickups and sick days.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫也全力支持接送孩子和处理孩子生病请假的事宜。

sentences.en: And at the same time, she gets word that a colleague is about to go out on maternity leave.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，她得到消息，有一位同事即将休产假。

sentences.en: And she sees this as a chance to prove just how committed she is to her job.
sentences.zh: 她把这视为一个机会，来证明自己对工作的承诺。

sentences.en: I just looked at it as, this is great.
sentences.zh: 我当时只想，这太棒了。

sentences.en: I'm going to prove to them that having this baby has not changed me.
sentences.zh: 我要向他们证明，生下这个孩子并没有改变我。

sentences.en: I wanted to show them that you can still rely on me.
sentences.zh: 我想向他们表明，你依然可以依赖我。

sentences.en: Nothing's going to change, you know.
sentences.zh: 一切都不会改变，你知道的。

sentences.en: And then when she went on her maternity leave, I said, I will cover her.
sentences.zh: 然后当她去休产假时，我说，我来接替她的工作。

sentences.en: I will do her job.
sentences.zh: 我来做她的工作。

sentences.en: I'll do both jobs.
sentences.zh: 两份工作我都做。

sentences.en: It's fine.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: So when you go back, you're working even harder than before.
sentences.zh: 所以当你回去的时候，你的工作比以前更拼了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And was there any recognition that you had done the work essentially of two people?
sentences.zh: 有没有人认可你实际上承担了两个人的工作？

sentences.en: Not particularly, no.
sentences.zh: 并没有特别的认可，没有。

sentences.en: I saw several times other people, other men particularly, or, you know, younger women without children be given opportunities.
sentences.zh: 我好几次看到其他人，尤其是其他男性，或者没有孩子的年轻女性获得了机会。

sentences.en: You know, whether it's like a move to another desk or a move up to a new role.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无论是调到另一个交易台还是晋升到新的岗位。

sentences.en: You know, I was seeing this happen all around me, but I was never asked, you know, even though every year I would put in my review that I wanted more leadership.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我看着这一切在身边发生，但我从未被问及过，尽管我每年都会在年终评估中写明我想要更多的领导机会。

sentences.en: I wanted to grow my career.
sentences.zh: 我想要拓展自己的职业生涯。

sentences.en: I mean, it was in there every single year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，年年都写在里面。

sentences.en: It was never brought up to me.
sentences.zh: 但从来没人跟我提起过。

sentences.en: And then she decides to have another kid.
sentences.zh: 然后她决定要第二个孩子。

sentences.en: So in 2016, I got pregnant with my second son.
sentences.zh: 所以在2016年，我怀上了第二个儿子。

sentences.en: And at one point, there was a BBC article that was published, and it was something about a woman's brain being impacted by pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 有一次，BBC发表了一篇文章，大意是说女性的大脑会受到怀孕的影响。

sentences.en: And the head trader stood up and looked right at me and, hey, the most read article today on the BBC is how women's brains are impacted by pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 首席交易员站起来，直盯着我说道：嘿，BBC今天阅读量最高的一篇文章是关于女性大脑如何受到怀孕影响的。

sentences.en: And, you know, loud enough that, I mean, I work in a trading floor, so everybody can hear everything.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，声音大得，我的意思是，我在交易大厅工作，所以每个人都能听到一切。

sentences.en: And it was humiliating, you know?
sentences.zh: 这真的很羞辱人，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It was like confirming that as a mother, I was somehow less than.
sentences.zh: 这就像是在证实，作为一个母亲，我不知为何就低人一等。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: What you're describing is kind of essentially grinning and bearing this behavior.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的基本上就是强颜欢笑、默默忍受这种行为。

sentences.en: And I wonder if at some point in this second pregnancy,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，在第二次怀孕的某个阶段，

sentences.en: you're more conscious of how all this is impacting you and if you start to feel like doing something more than just tolerating it.
sentences.zh: 你是否更清楚地意识到这一切对你产生了什么影响，你是否开始觉得自己想做点什么，而不仅仅是容忍？

sentences.en: And, you know, when I sat down in my review, you know, I brought up, I said, I haven't really been given any opportunities.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当我坐下来进行年终评估时，我提到了这一点，我说，我真的没有得到任何机会。

sentences.en: And she said that really the only way that I could, you know, increase my earning potential was to move laterally into an operations role like on another desk, which I pointed out,
sentences.zh: 她说我能提高赚钱潜力的唯一方法，就是平级调动到一个运营岗位，比如去另一个交易台，对此我指出，

sentences.en: well, that's a lateral move.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那只是平级调动。

sentences.en: You know, that's not really growing my career.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并没有真正拓展我的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And she said, well, you know, you should really think about something like that, though, because as a mom of two, you'll probably feel more comfortable, you know,
sentences.zh: 她说，好吧，你知道，你确实应该考虑一下这样的事情，因为作为一个有两个孩子的母亲，你可能会觉得更舒服，你知道，

sentences.en: staying where you are, being comfortable in what you know.
sentences.zh: 保持现状，在自己熟悉的事情上感到舒适。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It feels like this boss is telling you that you're supposed to accept this plateauing,
sentences.zh: 感觉这位老板是在告诉你，你应该接受这种职业停滞，

sentences.en: even though you've organized your life from everything you've said around making sure that having a family doesn't impact your work, which theoretically you don't even have to do,
sentences.zh: 尽管根据你所说的一切，你已经把生活安排得井井有条，确保组建家庭不会影响工作，理论上你甚至不需要做到这一步，

sentences.en: but you've decided to do.
sentences.zh: 但你还是决定这么做了。

sentences.en: And yet everyone at work is treating you as if you're not in a position to grow.
sentences.zh: 然而，工作中的每个人对待你的态度，都好像你没有晋升空间一样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Erin, is this starting to feel to you like discrimination?
sentences.zh: 艾琳，你开始觉得这是歧视了吗？

sentences.en: It's always felt like discrimination.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得这就是歧视。

sentences.en: Always.
sentences.zh: 一直都觉得。

sentences.en: I mean, I just think that I wanted so badly to not be one of the people impacted by discrimination.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我只是太渴望不成为受歧视影响的人之一了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: You know, like, I just, it was so obvious.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像，这太明显了。

sentences.en: I mean, if I talk to any of my female friends in the industry, it's like, yeah, duh, you decided to become a mom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我和业内任何女性朋友交谈，大家都会觉得，废话，你决定要当妈了嘛。

sentences.en: I wanted so badly to be somebody who could overcome it and not be impacted by it.
sentences.zh: 我极其渴望成为那种能够克服困难、不受其影响的人。

sentences.en: And in your mind, you were not able to defy those odds?
sentences.zh: 而在你看来，你没能打破这些偏见吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: It's just, it's just not, does not even seem possible.
sentences.zh: 这根本，根本就不像是可能的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你的第一个月应用体验是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用，即可免费畅读30天。

sentences.en: It sounds like for Erin, this was an accumulation of mostly subtle things, a few not so subtle, but largely subtle things.
sentences.zh: 听起来对Erin来说，这是一些大多很微妙的事情的积累，也有少数不太微妙的，但主要是很微妙的事情。

sentences.en: Abasa's comment about pregnant women directed at a large group of people she happens to be in, getting passed over for a set of promotions.
sentences.zh: Abasa针对孕妇的言论是针对她恰好所在的一大群人，结果她错失了一系列晋升机会。

sentences.en: All these things could definitely signal that a company was discriminating against her for being pregnant.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情绝对都可以表明，一家公司因为她怀孕而对她进行歧视。

sentences.en: But potentially they could just signal a poorly organized company, an insensitive company, and not really represent outright pregnancy discrimination.
sentences.zh: 但潜在地，它们可能只是表明一家组织混乱的公司、一家麻木不仁的公司，并不真正代表赤裸裸的怀孕歧视。

sentences.en: So how knowable is it that a situation like this stems from pregnancy discrimination?
sentences.zh: 那么，像这样的一种情况源于怀孕歧视，究竟有多大可能是可知的呢？

sentences.en: It is very difficult to know, but what we did for this story was talk to woman after woman, and we talked to women in very different workplaces.
sentences.zh: 这很难知道，但我们为这篇报道所做的是，采访了一位又一位女性，而且我们采访的是身处截然不同职场的女性。

sentences.en: We talked to a lot of white-collar women and blue-collar women.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了许多白领女性和蓝领女性。

sentences.en: And what we found was the same things kept cropping up over and over again.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现的是，同样的事情一遍又一遍地不断浮现。

sentences.en: There was a woman who was doing sales for Novartis, whose boss suggested that she get an abortion after she told him that she was pregnant.
sentences.zh: 有一位在诺华公司做销售的女性，在告诉老板自己怀孕后，她的老板建议她去堕胎。

sentences.en: There was a woman at Merck who was fired three weeks before she gave birth, even though she'd been a star, getting excellent performance reviews before she got pregnant.
sentences.zh: 默克公司有一位女性在她分娩前三周被解雇，尽管她曾是一名明星员工，在怀孕前获得了极好的绩效评估。

sentences.en: When you see the patterns that we saw appear, you begin to get the sense that pregnancy becomes a problem for a lot of employers.
sentences.zh: 当你看到我们所看到的这些模式出现时，你开始感觉到怀孕对许多雇主来说成了一个问题。

sentences.en: And you just need to look at the statistics to see that becoming a mom in the American workforce means you're taking a big hit.
sentences.zh: 你只需看一看统计数据就会发现，在美国职场成为母亲意味着你要承受沉重的打击。

sentences.en: And what do those statistics show?
sentences.zh: 这些统计数据说明了什么？

sentences.en: The data shows that women and men, their salaries rise in lockstep with one another until they have their first kid.
sentences.zh: 数据显示，女性和男性的薪资步调一致地同步上涨，直到他们有了第一个孩子。

sentences.en: And then men continue to rise and women decline.
sentences.zh: 然后男性的薪资继续上涨，而女性则下降。

sentences.en: For men, when you have a kid, you get a 6% pay bump.
sentences.zh: 对男性而言，当你有了孩子，你会获得6%的加薪。

sentences.en: For women, each pregnancy shaves 4% off of their salary.
sentences.zh: 对女性而言，每一次怀孕都会让她们的薪水减少4%。

sentences.en: Some of the problem is not about perceptions.
sentences.zh: 部分问题与观念无关。

sentences.en: It's about how child care and family responsibilities work in America, which is that women are still doing the bulk of that.
sentences.zh: 它关乎美国的育儿和家庭责任是如何运作的，那就是女性仍然在承担其中的大部分工作。

sentences.en: And so there are absences from work that explain some of that salary decline when women have kids.
sentences.zh: 因此，正是因为缺勤工作，才解释了女性生育后部分薪资下降的原因。

sentences.en: Meaning a mom might actually take time off of work, which represents lost wages.
sentences.zh: 这意味着妈妈们实际上可能会请假离开工作岗位，这就代表着工资的损失。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it doesn't explain all of it.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能解释全部。

sentences.en: So Stanford researchers sent out 1,200 resumes to prospective employers, and they were all female job candidates.
sentences.zh: 因此，斯坦福大学的研究人员向潜在雇主发送了1,200份简历，而且他们全都是女性求职者。

sentences.en: They were identical resumes, except that half of them indicated that the woman was a mother.
sentences.zh: 这些简历完全相同，只是其中一半表明这名女性是一位母亲。

sentences.en: The managers were twice as likely to call back the childless woman.
sentences.zh: 经理们回电给无子女女性的可能性是前者的两倍。

sentences.en: So why are childless women more attractive to hire to managers than mothers?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么对经理们来说，没有孩子的女性比母亲更有招聘吸引力呢？

sentences.en: It seems, according to, again, decades of research on this, that visibly pregnant women in one study, evaluators rated them as less reliable, less dependent, less competent.
sentences.zh: 根据再次说明，对此数十年的研究表明，在一项研究中，评估人员认为明显怀孕的女性更不可靠、更不独立、能力更差。

sentences.en: So this is where the perception aligns or intersects with the pay question.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是观念与薪酬问题相契合或交织的地方。

sentences.en: Because if someone is perceived as a less able worker, then managers will be less likely to hire them, give them pay raises, give them promotion opportunities.
sentences.zh: 因为如果一个人被认为是一个能力较差的员工，那么经理们就不太可能雇用他们、给他们加薪、给他们晋升机会。

sentences.en: What the sociologists have found is that when you have this responsibility at home, employers think that that will be the number one priority in your life.
sentences.zh: 社会学家发现，当你在家里承担这种责任时，雇主会认为这将是你生活中的头等大事。

sentences.en: And how could you prioritize us, your employer, as much as your kid?
sentences.zh: 你怎么可能像优先对待你的孩子那样优先对待我们这些雇主呢？

sentences.en: And men don't face that perception.
sentences.zh: 而男性则不会面临这种看法。

sentences.en: It almost sounds like companies are preemptively punishing mothers before they're given a chance to show that they, in fact, do want to work hard.
sentences.zh: 这听起来几乎像是公司在母亲们有机会证明自己实际上确实想努力工作之前，就先发制人地惩罚她们。

sentences.en: They do want to be promoted.
sentences.zh: 她们确实想要获得晋升。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Whereas men, when they have kids, companies are giving them a pay raise, right?
sentences.zh: 而男性在有了孩子后，公司会给他们加薪，对吧？

sentences.en: That's 6% pay bump.
sentences.zh: 那是6%的薪资涨幅。

sentences.en: What's that about?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么回事？

sentences.en: The sociologists say that comes from the perception that when men have a kid, they are going to be the breadwinner and they need to be able to care for a family.
sentences.zh: 社会学家表示，这来自于这样一种观念：当男性有了孩子后，他们将成为顶梁柱，并且需要能够照顾家庭。

sentences.en: So it's a boost for them.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他们来说是一个提升。

sentences.en: So everything you're describing seems to be based on a set of assumptions that a mother's productivity declines.
sentences.zh: 因此，你所描述的一切似乎都基于一系列假设，即母亲的生产力会下降。

sentences.en: Is that actually true?
sentences.zh: 这真的是真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's not true.
sentences.zh: 是的，这不是真的。

sentences.en: I mean, the research shows that women don't become less productive when they have kids.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，研究表明女性在有了孩子后并没有变得生产力低下。

sentences.en: In fact, it shows that mothers and fathers are more productive workers.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它表明母亲和父亲都是生产力更高的员工。

sentences.en: So this isn't based on some very real and rational assessment that all of a sudden mothers are going to start costing the company money because they're not as dedicated.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是基于某种非常真实和理性的评估，即母亲们会突然开始让公司付出金钱代价，因为她们没有那么投入。

sentences.en: That just doesn't bear out in the research.
sentences.zh: 这一点在研究中根本站不住脚。

sentences.en: Natalie, where is Erin Murphy now?
sentences.zh: 娜塔莉，Erin Murphy现在在哪里？

sentences.en: So Erin filed a lawsuit against Glencore earlier this month.
sentences.zh: 所以Erin在本月早些时候对嘉能可提起了一起诉讼。

sentences.en: She's suing for gender discrimination and pregnancy discrimination.
sentences.zh: 她正在以性别歧视和怀孕歧视起诉。

sentences.en: And she's still working at the company.
sentences.zh: 而且她仍然在这家公司工作。

sentences.en: It's obviously a little awkward.
sentences.zh: 这显然有点尴尬。

sentences.en: Do you think that any of these lawsuits from Otisha, from Erin, that they stand a chance of actually changing the situation for pregnant women and for mothers at work?
sentences.zh: 你认为来自Otisha、来自Erin的这些诉讼中，有任何一个是真正有机会改变职场中孕妇和母亲们的处境的吗？

sentences.en: I think we all watched the Me Too movement happen over the last year.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大家都目睹了过去一年发生的“我也是”（Me Too）运动。

sentences.en: And that is about women not being harassed and not being discriminated against at the workplace.
sentences.zh: 那是关于女性在职场中不被骚扰、不被歧视的。

sentences.en: But I wonder if you think that this problem of discrimination against pregnant women and mothers is in some ways more entrenched than that and potentially even harder to counteract.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道你是否认为，这种针对孕妇和母亲的歧视问题在某些方面比那更根深蒂固，甚至可能更难以对抗。

sentences.en: So I'm not sure that the legal battles, while important, are going to solve this problem,
sentences.zh: 所以我不确定法律斗争虽然重要，但能否解决这个问题，

sentences.en: because what we're talking about is really a cultural understanding of what's acceptable treatment and what isn't, of what's egregiously bad and what's just sort of subtle slights.
sentences.zh: 因为我们所讨论的实际上是对什么是可接受的对待、什么不是，什么是令人发指的糟糕、什么只是某种微妙轻视的文化理解。

sentences.en: And until there is a kind of broad reframing, like we saw with the Me Too movement, where, remember,
sentences.zh: 除非出现一种广泛的重塑，就像我们在“我也是”运动中所看到的那样，在那场运动中，请记住，

sentences.en: a lot of the behaviors that now we all are agreeing are unacceptable and egregious were things that were given a pass before this moment of consciousness raising where, you know,
sentences.zh: 许多现在我们都一致认为不可接受且令人发指的行为，在唤醒意识的这一时刻之前是被网开一面的，当时你知道，

sentences.en: the bounds of what's considered okay have changed.
sentences.zh: 被认为可以接受的界限已经改变了。

sentences.en: You know, the goalposts have changed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，目标已经改变了。

sentences.en: Until we see that kind of fundamental shift when it comes to how corporate America views pregnant people and mothers,
sentences.zh: 在我们看到企业美国对待孕妇和母亲的看法发生这种根本性转变之前，

sentences.en: I don't think you're going to see a broad kind of change that affects more people than the ones that are covered by these lawsuits.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你会看到一种广泛的改变，能够影响到比这些诉讼所涵盖的人更多的人。

sentences.en: Aaron, has this whole experience felt like your employer, and in some sense a larger world, made you choose?
sentences.zh: Aaron，这段经历是否让你觉得你的雇主，并在某种意义上更大的世界，让你做出选择？

sentences.en: You can either be committed to your career or you can be committed to your family, but not both.
sentences.zh: 要么你可以致力于你的职业生涯，要么你可以致力于你的家庭，但不能两者兼得。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At Glencore for sure.
sentences.zh: 在嘉能可绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: I just, I came in almost six years ago with so much hope and so much, so much to offer, and I honestly feel like I've taken a step backwards.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我将近六年前带着如此多的希望和如此多的、如此多的贡献来到这里，我老实说觉得自己倒退了一步。

sentences.en: I can't not say anything anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不能再什么都不说了。

sentences.en: I can't be silent anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不能再沉默了。

sentences.en: Being silent is allowing this to happen.
sentences.zh: 保持沉默就是纵容这种事的发生。

sentences.en: Aaron, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: Aaron，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周在《裁切器》（The Wirecutter）节目中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让你的客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是遮光睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是为了睡觉而昏过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、对食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用上或在你喜欢收听的任何地方寻找《裁切器》节目。
